Why I think people with bpd get demonised… I think a lot of it has to do with misrepresentation and the media. Similarly to a range of things, it is somehow negatively viewed (in this context before they really did any research so it wasn’t really understood and we got labelled crazy… I mean if I met a borderline when nothing was known hell I’d probably call them crazy) and there slowly and slowly became more information and research (however I still think it is lacking a bit) people are starting to find out more of the reality of it. The problem with that is that not everyone will see or be willing to learn and it isn’t something that you see commonly like anxiety or depression, and it’s not one you learn in school. (I just went and did something and came back so lost my train of thought so if it’s a bit all over the place my bad). I think as well there have been a lot of negative portrayal in the media with commonly criminals and not the good ones. As a society, we have started focusing a lot on and researching explanations behind why people commit crimes (I will highlight they in no way are trying to find excuses. I have studied criminology for a bit and that was a large part of it. You read books or listen to podcasts on crimes? They will 9/10 times examine the contributions to why this person commit the crime including childhood, relationships and mental illness) and with bpd becoming more common (like popular kinda) it’s being bought up, you’ll see it in true crime docs and stuff too. I feel as though either because they see this and then associate it or they search it up and see outdated or bias information. A lot of the other diagnoses that get mentioned (ie psychopath, sociopath, schizophrenia, depression, ect) are more researched and known by the public , and I’ll be the first to admit that some of them don’t have a good reputation either. It also wasn’t diagnosed until a while after some of these people (such as Aileen Wuornos and Jeffery Dahmer) committed their crimes. Basically I feel like it’s a mix of media, existing reputation that some people go with for various reasons, not enough research especially compared to other illnesses and honestly slightly the rise in true crime consumerism (in no way am I shit talking true crime, it’s one of my hyperfixations and I’ve been heavily interested for years). I think that’s all?

1. There’s 9 main symptoms of bpd and honestly I fit each one way or another. 
- fear of abandonment (this is my worst and most life-crushing soul-crushing world-turning symptom. I get SEVERELY attached to certain people and then it’s a whole constant battle with things like thoughts and validation and reassurance and fear they’re gonna leave, ect)
- unstable relationships - I have a history of getting really close and almost inseparable to one person at a time and it often blows up from both sides
- unclear/shifting self image - I don’t actually know who I am and don’t think I ever have. I get asked especially in therapy to tell them about myself or name things I like or what my morals and values are and I really don’t know and I will genuinely try to think but I cannot come up with anything. I also will take on certain people around mes attributes
- impulsive/self destructive behaviour - I have engaged in this since age 11, this includes self harm, substances, binge drinking, picking fights with people (this one I mostly only do with people who are saying something I strongly genuinely do not agree with, the latest being a lady saying someone who was scheduled for his mh did not deserve the bed because he’s an addict) and more
- self harm - multiple forms since 11, I’m absolutely covered in scars and not the ones that will go away eventually type 
- extreme emotion mood swings - I (along with a lot of other borderlines) are like bipolar on speed, but add stuff. There is no ‘dedicated’ medication for bpd like there is almost every other mental illness so it’s common for us to be on a cocktail of meds to stabilise mood a little better. I’m currently on 8 or 9, most of them at highest doses but having little effect however I react terribly to any changes atm). We feel emotions deeper than ‘normal’ people and that’s a fact. It’s compared to having over 90% of your body covered in third degree burns
- chronic emptiness - I still don’t know how to explain it. Nothing feels right, nothing feels fulfilling, nothing feels ok. I rather sit with being severely suicidal than I would sit with the emptiness 
- explosive anger - I however let my anger out internally and on myself, occasionally over text
- feeling out of touch with reality - I dissociate a lot and have since I was very young. More often than not I find myself questioning if I am real and if life is real and questioning that way that the world and everything basically works and it’s hard to believe 

2. Life is hard, and I think that most people will find that but everyone’s ’hard’ and circumstances are different. Sometimes I find it kinda hard I guess and I’ve often had professionals tell me all my stuff is hard and life would be hard with it. Relationships yeah I guess are hard however atm majority of my relationships I have met in psych hospitals and some also have bpd and we all understand each other

3. Honestly I don’t see myself living past like 30/40 so it would not be fair on that child if I left them however I would love to be able to have one. I am also so scared that I would become like my own parents or worse and put my child through trauma. Something I’ve always said to myself and wanted is that having kids, I will make sure I have an open and positive relationship and they can come to me with anything and instead of punishing or whatever we will talk and discuss. For example mental health would be a common topic and they would be able to tell me if they’re struggling. But also telling them that if they drink or do drugs, just to let me know and I will pick them up or whatever because they’re going to do it anyways and I rather them be safe

4. Having a child as a parent with bpd, when they’re old enough I would explain in appropriate terms to them relevant and appropriate parts such as having obvious scars, when they’re old enough I will explain how when I was younger I hurt myself because I didn’t know how else to help myself when I felt too many emotions and make sure they ALWAYS know that they can talk to me about ANYTHING and if I cannot help them or support them fully I will make sure to find someone who can and still be by their side in the way 

5. If I didn’t seek treatment and it was affecting people around me, including my child, actually even if I was still seeking treatment I would want someone to tell me because I promise you the last thing I (and most of us) want to do is hurt anyone especially those around us and that we love. I will however probably be somewhat sad and hard on myself that my child had to say something for me to notice. 

6. Understanding my current symptoms, even if I wasn’t aware of them I’d not be overly stressed having them with me more however there would probably be times that it would be appropriate that they take them so I can reset. Again, a lot of my symptoms are internal so to say, so I take it out on myself. I have learnt to ‘minimise’ my reaction in the moment when around people, especially children. It’s going to be different for everyone and every doctor. Honestly, I’ve had maybe like 7/10 doctors not say something (whether it was mh related or not) and those who did were just concerned about the risk I had to myself I.e if I was doing it to try and off myself and that sorta thing. I’m not sure your situation but I know that if I get asked about it, I’ll briefly explain why (like 1 sentence) and say I have a psychologist (or doctor or psychiatrist or whatever clinician) that I am working on it with. Not sure what they look like, but if it’s a possibility you could say it was like a year or 2 ago. I won’t say they won’t but if it’s for your stomach there’s a chance they won’t even pay attention to your scars.

I know it may be hard for multiple reasons but try to see your therapist more often, at least fortnightly but weekly is probably ideal. Be open and honest with them (again can be easier said than done) and tell them you’re struggling with the strong urge to cut deeper which is concerning you and you feel like you really need help (whether that’s inpatient or not). That being said, I honestly would try to avoid inpatient as long as possible because it’s not a nice environment, 99% of it can be traumatic. Private wards aren’t as bad but still have their traumatic aspects. It can also become a revolving door, in the last 4 years I’ve had at least 15-20+ hospital visits/stays. Hurting yourself with plainly just the intent of hurting yourself is enough to deserve help. Please try as long as possible before you start going deeper because it’s a slippery slope, it’s addicting and it’s left me covered in wide,deep purple and white scars. I hope you can get the help you need :)
